rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR A P125 DAILY ACROSS-THE-BOAR D INCREASE IN THE WAGE AND SALARY RATES OF EMPLOYEES AND WORKERS IN THE PRIVATE SECTOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: This bill provides that all employers in the private sector, whether agricultural or non-agricultura l, regardless of capitalization and number of employees shall pay their workers an across-the-boar d wage increase in the sum of One Hundred TwentyFive pesos (P125.00) a day upon the effectivity of this Act. > No wage incrase shall be credited as compliance with the increase prescribed herein unless expressly provided under valid collective bargaining agreements; provided, that such wage increase was granted in anticipation of the legislated across-the-boar d wage increase under the Act; and, provided further, that where such increase is less than the prescribed increase under this Act, the employer shall pay the difference. Such increasess shall not include anniversary wage increases, merit wage increases and those resulting from the regularization or promotion of employees.
rows.status: Substituted by HB04188

rows.author: D084
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR A THREE THOUSAND PESOS (P3,000.00) ACROSS-THE-BOAR D MONTHLY SALARY INCREASE IN THE WAGE AND SALARY RATES OF EMPLOYEES AND WORKERS IN THE PUBLIC SECTOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: As provided, an across-the-boar d monthly salary increase of three thousand pesos (P3,000) shall be granted to all employees, whether permanent, temporary, emergency, contractual or casual of the National Government, its agencies and instrumentalities including the Local Government Units. > This piece of legislation intends to provide the much-needed economic relief to an important section of the bureaucracy - the rank-and-file employees. This intention should be carried out through the provision of a P3,000 across-the-boar d salary increase to all public sector employees.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on APPROPRIATIONS since 2001-08-27

rows.title_full: AN ACT MANDATING EMPLOYERS TO GRANT UP TO FOUR (4) WEEKS OF UNPAID LEAVE A YEAR TO EMPLOYEES WHOSE SPOUSE, PARENT, UNMARRIED CHILD, OR WHEN THEY THEMSELVES ARE SUFFERING FROM SERIOUS ILLNESS
rows.abstract: "Family and Medical Leave Act of 2001". An employee whether employed in the private sector or government entity may apply for a Family and Medical Leave when his legitimate spouse, parent, or legitimate unmarried child suffers from a serious illness.  The employee may also apply for the same if he himself is physically unable to perform his job due to a serious illness.  A casual or temporary employee can avail of the benefits of this Act only after twelve (12) months of continuous employment with the same employer.  The employee availing of the benefits of this Act shall be reinstated to his original position with equivalent pay, benefits and all other term and conditions of employment upon return.
rows.status: Substituted by HB05432

rows.abstract: All retired Filipino government personnel shall be given free medical services in government-owne d and -operated hospitals. In reality, upon the retirement of these public servants, they are left with insufficient support and benefits that slowly devaluate. While the costs of living through their retirement increase, financial support to answer to their medical needs decrease in value as well.

rows.title_full: AN ACT GRANTING P125.00 DAILY AGROSS-THE-BOAR D IN WAGES OF FILIPINO WORKERS NATIONWIDE
rows.abstract: Rationale: Worker's wages have already been severely eroded and devaluated many times over the series of oil price increases since the oil deregulation policy was implemented. The recent oil price increase further deteriorated the adverse situationand triggered unrest among the working class.  Beyond doubt, there is a need to reset wages as oil prices continue to erode the purchasing power of the consuming public. > A P125.00 daily across-the-boar d wage increase will be granted to all Filipino workers nationwide in view of the rising costs of living in the country.
rows.status: Substituted by HB04188

rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING SECTION 31 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7166, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS `AN ACT PROVIDING FOR SYNCHRONIZED NATIONAL AND LOCAL ELECTIONS AND FOR ELECTORAL REFORMS, AUTHORIZING APPROPRIATIONS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES' TO INCLUDE HAZARD ALLOWANCE AND LIFE INSURANCE BENEFITS AS ADDITIONAL BENEFITS FOR MEMBERS OF THE BOARD OF ELECTION INSPECTORS AND OTHER OFFICIALS
rows.abstract: The Board of Election Inspectors SHALL BE ENTITLED TO ONE THOUSAND PESOS (P1,000.00) AS HAZARD ALLOWANCE EACH FOR SERVICES ON THE DAY OF ELECTION. THEY SHALL BE COVERED BY AN INSURANCE POLICY FOR DEATH OR INJURY SUSTAINED WHILE IN THE PERFORMANCE OFTHEIR DUTY, OR BY REASON THEREOF: PROVIDED, THAT IN CASE OF DEATH, THE AMOUNT OF ONE HUNDRED THOUSAND PESOS (P100,000.00) SHALL BE PAID TO THEIR PRIMARY BENEFICIARIES, AND IN THE ABSENCE THEREOF, TO THEIR LEGAL HEIRS: PROVIDED, FURTHER THAT IN CASEOF ANY INJURY, THE DEPARTMENT OF EDUCATION, CULTURE AND SPORTS OR THE COMMISSION SHALL PROVIDE FOR THE SCHEDULE OF COMPENSATION WHICH, IN NO CASE, SHALL BE LESS THAN TEN THOUSAND PESOS (P10,000.00), NOR MORE THAN ONE HUNDRED THOUSAND PESOS (P100,000..00).> PRIMARY BENEFICIARIES AS MENTIONED IN THIS ACT SHALL REFER TO THE LAWFUL SPOUSE, AND THEIR CHILD/CHILDREN. IN THE ABSENCE THEREOF, TO PERSONS, WHO UNDER EXISTING LAWS, ARE ENTITLED TO SUCCEED.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on SUFFRAGE AND ELECTORAL REFORMS since 2001-08-28

rows.title_full: AN ACT TO AMEND SUBSECTION (C) OF SECTION SEVENTY-THREE AND SECTION SEVENTY-FOUR OF REPUBLIC ACT NUMBERED SIX THOUSAND SIX HUNDRED AND FIFTY-SEVEN, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE `COMPREHENSIVE AGRARIAN REFORM LAW OF 1988,' AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: This bill seeks to amend Section 73 (c) and Section 74 of Republic Act No. 6657, otherwise known as the "Comprehensive Agrarian Reform Law of 1988" and consider as protected areas for food production all agricultural lands with existing irrigation facilities or with funding commitment for an irrigation facility.  For this purpose, therefore, it shall be prohibited and non-negotiable for conversion into non-agricultura l uses, such residential or those agricultural lands having funding commitment for an irrigation facility. Such conversions have brought about adverse effects on our food security and food production program of the government, particularly rice.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on AGRARIAN REFORM since 2001-08-28

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE ESTABLISHMENT OF HUMAN RIGHTS ACTION CENTERS IN ALL THE LEGISLATIVE DISTRICTS AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: The incidence of human rights violation have considerably decreased since the creation of the Commission on Human Rights under the administration of former President Corazon C. Aquino as embodied in the 1987 Constitution, but due to lack of manpowerand adequate resources, there are still a number of isolated cases of human rights violations especially in the rural and remote areas where the government could not provide for enough protection for the people to enjoy a just and humane life.  In acivilized society like the Philippines, violations of human rights have no place and should be curved by the State at all cost. > This bill will provide the necessary assistance to the people who have been victimized by government officials and emplloyees. This will encourage them to report cases of violation to the Human Righst Action Center that will provide them the necessary legal assistance, protection and security.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on CIVIL, POLITICAL AND HUMAN RIGHTS since 2001-08-28

rows.author: C005
rows.title_full: AN ACT REQUIRING ALL CANDIDATES FOR ELECTIVE POSITIONS IN GOVERNMENT AND ALL APPOINTIVE PUBLIC OFFICIALS TO UNDERGO MANDATORY AND PERIODIC DRUG TESTING
rows.abstract: This bill seeks to require all candidates for any elective position, as a prerequisite to the filing of their certificates of candidacy, and all appointive public officials in the upper echelon of the bureaucratic hierarchy to undergo drug test. > There is no graver threat than drug traffickers and drug users infiltrating the mainstream of the government bureaucracy. The government must implement a policy that would effectively detect and prevent drug users and abusers from entering the mainstream of public service. Hence, the State must ensure that only competent, qualified and drug-free people are elected and/or appointed to public office.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on SUFFRAGE AND ELECTORAL REFORMS since 2001-08-28

rows.author: D001
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING BENEFITS TO ANY PERSON WHO DIED OR SUSTAINED INJURY WHILE TRYING TO PREVENT THE COMMISSION OF A CRIME OR WHILE COMING TO THE AID OR RESCUE OF A VICTIM OR VICTIMS OF A CRIME AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: "Good Samaritan Act".  As used in this Act, the term "Good Samaritan" refers to any person who while not being a member of any law enforcement agency, dies or sustains injury while trying to prevent the commission of a crime or while coming to the aid or rescue of a victim or victims of a crime. > This bill therefore, seeks to provide compensation to any person who died or sustained injury while trying to prevent the commission of a crime or crimes or who comes to the aid of or rescues victimsof a crime. This bill not only accord due recognition and assistance to those who have risked their life and limb at stake but will also encourage the people to perform their civic duties as citizens.

rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A PROVIDENT PERSONAL SAVINGS PLAN KNOWN AS THE `PERSONAL EQUITY AND RETIREMENT ACCOUNT'
rows.abstract: Rationale: Since almost all people look forward to retirement as a moment when they will finally be able to relax and enjoy the pleasure of having more time for themselves and their families away from the pressures of daily work, the Philippine Government takes the responsibility of providing a better life for the retirees of our society in line with its Constitutional mandate. However, without a dependable retirement plan, they are not assured a comfortable and leisurely retirement. >This proposed measure seeks to introduce the Personal Equity and Retirement Account (PERA) which we hope will be accepted as an essential and valuable tool in encouraging savings for our people's retirement years by providing a financially-sec ure retirementthrough a sound investment and planning scheme through savings, and a flexible and dynamic investment scheme that will benefit a good part of our working populace who are neither members of government funds and who have very limited options.
rows.status: Substituted by HB06001

rows.mother_status: Approved by the House on 2002-12-17, transmitted to on 2002-12-18 and received by the Senate on 2003-01-06
rows.title_full: AN ACT DECLARING ARNIS AS THE PHILIPPINE NATIONAL SPORT
rows.abstract: Rationale: Arnis is a sport that is indigenous and uniquely Filipino. Among the many games in the country, it can be considered as one of our national cultural gems that completely originated from the Philippines. This art was practiced primarily for self-defense by the Filipinos during the pre-Spanish period.  While during the Spanish period, Arnis was used to fight against the Spanish invaders.  The Filipinos stand against the superiorly armed adversaries in mortal combat in the areas of battle is now held in immortal inviolability by history. It would not be far-fetched to surmise that one of the earliest Filipino heroes, Lapu-Lapu, was an Arnis expert.

rows.abstract: Authority to use Domestic Letter of Credit. - All national government agencies (NGA) and government owned and/or controlled corporations (GOCC) are hereby authorized to use domestic letter of credit (DL/C) to pay for purchases from local suppliers through authorized government servicing banks (AGSB) under the terms and conditions specified hereunder. > Coverage. - This Act shall be applicable only for the procurement of supplies, materials and equipments. Authorizing the government to use domestic letter of credit to pay purchases from local suppliers enhances competition not only among themselves, but also between local and foreign ssuppliers. rows.abstract: Rationale:  In spite of laws enacted to implement agrarian reform in the country, the distribution of land to the landless farmers has yet to realize its goals. There are instances when farmer-benefici aries' titles or rights to the land were canceled due to the absence of tillers. Many farmer-benefici aries were forced by circumstances to mortgage their rights for temporary period, even on conditions that the mortgagee shall take over the possession and cultivation of the land.  It doesn't seem reasonable and equitable to cancel the title or rights of a farmer beneficiary who, by necessity, temporarily abandons the land awarded to him.  Thus, this bill.

rows.abstract: Any person holding and elective public office who is found guilty of political turncoatism as defined under this Act, after due notice and hearing, shall not be qualified for any elective position in any election immediately following the expirationof his term of office. > A candidate, other than the incumbent elective public official, who is likewise found guilty of political turncoatism, after due notice and hearing befire the Commission on Elections, shall not be qualified to run for any elective public office immediately following his change of political party affiliation. > In either case, any candidate, whether an incumbent elective public official or not, shall not be qualified to assume or hold any elective public office within thhe term of office immediately following the date of the elections from which he was disqualified to participate in violation of this Act.

rows.title_full: AN ACT DECLARING THE EXEMPTION OF THE JUDICIARY FROM THE COVERAGE OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 6758, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE SALARY STANDARDIZATION LAW
rows.abstract: Rationale: Corruption at all levels viciously undermines the integrity of the Judiciary. It compromises public faith and confidence in a system whose moral authority is its very foundation. The Judiciary has also been criticized for its sluggish disposition of cases. Also a major facotr contributing to the overwhelming case load is the lack of judges in many branches all over the country. This situation is disturbing considering the staggering number of active cases in our courts. Our judges and their staff are overworked and yet they do not receive a commensurate increase in their salaries. With the increase in work load, it is expected that Judiciary personnel should also received an increase in their salaries and benefits but such is noot the case. > It is the conviction of this representation that this problem can be partly addressed if we allow the Supreme Court to fix the salaries of judges and court personnel to a higher level that what is enjoyed today.

rows.author: A091
rows.title_full: AN ACT INCREASING THE PENALTIES FOR ILLEGAL LOGGING AND PENALIZING ILLEGAL IMPORTATION, SALE, RE-SALE, PURCHASE AND POSSESSION OF CHAINSAWS, AMENDING FOR THIS PURPOSE SECTION 68 OF PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NO. 705, AS AMENDED, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: The nation had reeled from the devastating effects of denuded forests. Throughout the country, thousands of lives and billions of pesos of properties were lost to flashfloods. We could still remember what happened to Ormoc and Nueva Ecija. > It is therefore of extreme urgency to add more teeth to our present forstly law by penalizing not judt the illegal possession of chainsaws but also it illegal importation, sale, re-sale and purchase. this measure could surely discourage indiscriminate exploitation of our dwindling forest reserves.
rows.status: Substituted by HB03994

rows.author: A091
rows.title_full: AN ACT EXEMPTING POOR LITIGANTS FROM POSTING BAIL WHEN CHARGED WITH NON-CAPITAL OFFENSES FOR THE FIRST TIME AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: "Poor Litigants Equalization Act of 2001". Any poor litigant who are citizens of the Philippines shall be exempt from posting bail when charged with non-capital offenses for the first time in any court in the Philippines and be released on his/her own recognizance except when the probability of flight is evident, as determined by the court.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2001-09-03

rows.author: A091
rows.title_full: AN ACT AUTHORIZING LOCAL GOVERNMENT UNITS TO UTILIZE THEIR ANNUAL INTERNAL REVENUE ALLOTMENT (IRA) AS COLLATERAL TO INCUR INDEBTEDNESS WITH ANY GOVERNMENT OR PRIVATE FINANCIAL INSTITUTION AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: This bill endeavors to provide part of the answer to the constant need of LGUs for money to finance, among others, their daily operation s and infrastructure needs. For LGUs to wait for the quarterly IRA releases as provided for by law may delay their response to ever-growing opportunities awaiting their respective localities. > It is the proposotion of this representation that LGUs be allowed to use thier share of their annual IRA as collateral to enable them to borrow funds from either government of private financial institutions for their development needs. However, such collateral must only be limited to the LGUs share of their annual IRA within the term of office for which they are elected.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2001-09-03

rows.author: D069
rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING THE AGRICULTURAL GUARANTY CORPORATION, PRESCRIBING ITS POWERS, FUNCTIONS AND DUTIES, PROVIDING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Among others, the proposed AGRICULTURAL CREDIT GUARANTY MECHANISM aims to: (1) To enhance the capability of low-income groups to acquire agricultural equipment, post harvet facilities, fertilizers, agriculture chemicals and other support mechanismsand facilities which shall render affordable such acquisitions; (2) To provide for a strong and sustainable agricultural credit program with complimentary support systems, which will pump prime, build-up and strengthen available sources of cheap andlong-term capital for agricultural development; (3) To encourage the flow of private funds for agricultural development and provide credit facilities and guarantee mechanism through a viable system of mortgage and credit quaranty; and (4) Serve the aagricultural requirements of all the underprivileged and those small farmers especially those who are not members of any funding agencies such as the Government SErvice and Insurance System (GSIS) and Social Security System (SSS).
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on GOVERNMENT ENTERPRISES AND PRIVATIZATION since 2001-09-03
